routing.description: API routing using Express Router with thin route-handler-service pattern. Next.js App Router file-based routing for storefront. Vite query-param routing for admin.

required_patterns.express-route-registration: All Express routes are registered as Router instances in packages/api/src/routes/ and mounted in app.ts via app.use(prefix, router)
required_patterns.handler-delegation: Routes delegate to handler functions in packages/api/src/handlers/. Handlers are thin wrappers that call service functions.
required_patterns.async-handler-wrapper: All async Express route handlers must be wrapped with asyncHandler() from utils/asyncHandler.ts to forward errors to error middleware
required_patterns.nextjs-api-proxy: Next.js API routes in apps/web/src/app/api/ act as proxies that forward requests to the Express API server

architectural_constraints.route-prefix-convention: Public API routes use /api/ prefix. Admin routes use /api/v1/admin/ prefix.
architectural_constraints.no-business-logic-in-routes: Route files only compose middleware chains. Zero business logic allowed in route files.
architectural_constraints.nextjs-proxy-only: apps/web API routes are BFF proxies only — they forward to packages/api and never contain direct DB access

auth.description: JWT-based authentication with role-based authorization (RBAC). Three roles: CUSTOMER, ADMIN, TAILOR.

required_patterns.jwt-bearer-auth: All authenticated routes use the authenticate middleware from packages/api/src/middleware/authenticate.ts. Token is extracted from Authorization: Bearer header.
required_patterns.role-based-authorization: Protected routes use authorize(...allowedRoles) middleware after authenticate. Roles are: CUSTOMER, ADMIN, TAILOR.
required_patterns.auth-rate-limiting: Auth endpoints (register, login) are rate-limited to 10 requests per 15 minutes per IP using express-rate-limit
required_patterns.password-hashing: Passwords are hashed with bcryptjs (10 salt rounds). AuthService is a static class pattern.
required_patterns.schema-validation-on-auth: Auth requests are validated using RegisterSchema and LoginSchema from @jhaz-imprints/shared

architectural_constraints.token-structure: JWT payload contains { id, email, role }. Tokens expire in 7 days.
architectural_constraints.middleware-order: authenticate must precede authorize in middleware chain. authorize must never be used without authenticate.
architectural_constraints.admin-routes-require-admin-role: All /api/v1/admin/* routes require ADMIN role via router.use(authenticate, authorize('ADMIN'))

data-layer.description: Dual-database architecture: PostgreSQL (Prisma) for transactional data and MongoDB (Mongoose) for flexible catalog data.

required_patterns.prisma-transactional: All financial operations (order creation + payment) use prisma.$transaction() for atomicity
required_patterns.prisma-singleton: Prisma client is a singleton exported from packages/db/src/client.ts with global caching to prevent connection exhaustion in development
required_patterns.mongoose-models: Mongoose models use typed schemas (Schema<IProduct>) with sub-schemas for nested objects. Models export from packages/catalog-db/src/models/
required_patterns.mongoose-paginate: Product listing uses mongoose-paginate-v2 plugin. Results capped at 50 per page.
required_patterns.mongodb-connection: MongoDB connects with exponential backoff retry (5 attempts). Connection pooling configured (maxPoolSize: 10, minPoolSize: 2).
required_patterns.lean-queries: All read-only MongoDB queries use .lean() for plain JS objects and .select('-__v') to exclude version key

architectural_constraints.transactional-in-postgres: Money, identity, and order data must live in PostgreSQL. Never store financial data in MongoDB.
architectural_constraints.flexible-in-mongodb: Product catalog, garment attributes, and image metadata belong in MongoDB for schema flexibility.
architectural_constraints.no-cross-db-transactions: No atomic transactions spanning both databases. Order service coordinates manually (create in PG first, then initialize payment).
architectural_constraints.idempotency-via-unique-constraints: Payment.reference has @unique constraint. Webhook handlers must check for existing completion before processing.

validation.description: Zod-based runtime validation shared between API and clients via @jhaz-imprints/shared package.

required_patterns.zod-schemas-in-shared: All API request/response schemas are Zod objects defined in packages/shared/src/schemas/. Types are inferred with z.infer<>.
required_patterns.validateBody-middleware: Express routes use validateBody(zodSchema) middleware to validate req.body. On failure, throws AppError with VALIDATION_ERROR code.
required_patterns.schema-reuse: Both frontend (React Hook Form with zodResolver) and backend (validateBody middleware) import the same schemas from @jhaz-imprints/shared

architectural_constraints.shared-schemas-are-source-of-truth: Zod schemas in packages/shared must not drift from Prisma models. Changes to schema.prisma require corresponding schema updates.
architectural_constraints.no-inline-validation: Request validation is never done inline in handlers. Always use validateBody middleware or zodResolver.

error-handling.description: Centralized error handling with typed AppError class and Express error middleware.

required_patterns.AppError-class: Custom AppError extends Error with statusCode and optional code. Constructed as new AppError(message, statusCode, code?).
required_patterns.isAppError-guard: Error middleware uses isAppError() type guard to distinguish operational errors from unexpected errors.
required_patterns.centralized-error-middleware: All errors are caught by the final Express error middleware in app.ts. AppErrors return structured { error, code }, generic errors return 500.
required_patterns.asyncHandler-wrapper: Async route handlers use asyncHandler() to automatically catch and forward Promise rejections to error middleware

architectural_constraints.no-try-catch-in-handlers: Handlers throw AppError; they do not catch and format errors themselves. The centralized middleware handles formatting.
architectural_constraints.exception-for-auth-handlers: Auth handlers (register, login) use local try-catch with manual status codes. This is a legacy pattern.

ui.description: Two separate frontend apps: Next.js 14 storefront (apps/web) with server components and Vite+React admin dashboard (apps/admin) with client-side only.

required_patterns.tailwind-utility-classes: All styling uses Tailwind CSS utility classes. Custom classes: card, input, btn-primary, btn-secondary, text-muted, text-error, bg-primary.
required_patterns.react-query-for-data: Both apps use @tanstack/react-query for data fetching. QueryClient is created at app root. Queries use queryKey arrays and queryFn.
required_patterns.react-hook-form-with-zod: Forms use useForm() with zodResolver(ZodSchema). useFieldArray for dynamic form sections.
required_patterns.localstorage-persistence: Auth tokens stored as 'auth_token'. User roles stored as 'user_role'. Wizard drafts stored as 'measurement_wizard_draft'.
required_patterns.step-wizard-pattern: Multi-step forms use numeric step state with const STEPS array. FormProvider wraps all steps.

architectural_constraints.admin-is-client-only: apps/admin is a Vite SPA — no server-side rendering. All data comes from API calls.
architectural_constraints.web-uses-server-components: apps/web defaults to server components. Client components must use 'use client' directive.
architectural_constraints.no-global-state: No Redux, Zustand, or Context API for global state. React Query handles server state, localStorage handles persistence.

notifications.description: Async notification pipeline using BullMQ job queue with Redis backing.

required_patterns.queue-job-pattern: Notification jobs are added via notificationQueue.add(jobName, jobData). Job names: 'order-confirmed', 'status-updated'.
required_patterns.worker-switch-dispatch: The BullMQ Worker uses a switch statement on job.name to dispatch to handler functions.
required_patterns.non-fatal-sends: Each email/notification send is wrapped in individual try-catch. One failure must never prevent other notifications from firing.
required_patterns.email-templates: HTML email templates are generated by pure functions in packages/api/src/integrations/email/templates.ts. All use inline CSS for email client compatibility.

architectural_constraints.redis-required: BullMQ requires Redis. Connection configured via REDIS_HOST and REDIS_PORT env vars.
architectural_constraints.retry-with-backoff: Jobs retry 3 times with exponential backoff (2s base delay).
architectural_constraints.email-only-channel: Current implementation supports email only via nodemailer (Gmail SMTP).

file-uploads.description: Image upload pipeline using Multer for parsing and Cloudinary for cloud storage.

required_patterns.multer-memory-storage: Files are parsed into memory buffers via multer.memoryStorage(). No disk storage.
required_patterns.cloudinary-stream-upload: Upload uses cloudinary.v2.uploader.upload_stream() with the buffer piped to the stream.
required_patterns.upload-response-shape: Successful uploads return { url, publicId, width, height }.
required_patterns.idempotent-delete: Cloudinary delete treats 'not found' as success (idempotent). Uses destroy(publicId).

architectural_constraints.5mb-limit: Max file size is 5 MB. Enforced by multer limits.
architectural_constraints.image-only: Only image/* MIME types accepted. Validated in multer fileFilter.
architectural_constraints.webp-conversion: All uploaded images are auto-converted to WebP format via Cloudinary format option.
architectural_constraints.folder-organization: All product images stored in 'jhaz-imprints/products/' folder on Cloudinary.
architectural_constraints.three-env-vars: Cloudinary requires CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME, CLOUDINARY_API_KEY, CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET. Never use CLOUDINARY_URL.

payments.description: Paystack payment integration for Nigerian Naira transactions.

required_patterns.initialize-verify-flow: Payment flow: Initialize (POST /transaction/initialize) → Customer pays on Paystack → Verify (GET /transaction/verify/{reference}).
required_patterns.kobo-conversion: Amounts are stored in Naira but converted to kobo (* 100) for Paystack API calls. Reversed on verification (/ 100).
required_patterns.idempotent-webhook: Webhook handler uses double-check locking: check outside transaction, re-check inside transaction. Prevents race conditions.

architectural_constraints.reference-uniqueness: Payment.reference is globally unique (format: order_{orderId}_{timestamp}). Used as idempotency key.
architectural_constraints.paystack-secret-required: PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY env var is required. App crashes at module load if missing.

testing.description: Unit testing with Vitest, comprehensive external service mocking.

required_patterns.vitest-with-global-setup: Tests run via vitest with setupFiles pointing to test-setup.ts. Global mocks for BullMQ, nodemailer, twilio, cloudinary.
required_patterns.mock-all-externals: All external services (Redis, email, SMS, cloud storage) are mocked at module scope in test-setup.ts to prevent real network calls.
required_patterns.test-file-location: Test files live alongside source in __tests__/ directories following *.test.ts pattern.

architectural_constraints.test-database-url: Tests use TEST_DATABASE_URL env var, overriding DATABASE_URL. Tests must never hit production database.
architectural_constraints.no-integration-tests-for-mongo: MongoDB operations are not covered by current test suite.
